messages.subject: Re: Error in occurrence query
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,
Thanks for bringing this to my attention. While I work on a fix so it doesn't crash Wallace, I recommend downloading your dataset directly from GBIF and using the User-specified module option. You can upload a dataset in .csv format with the first three columns/fields as "scientific_name", "longitude", and "latitude" (in that order). One of the entries for this species is causing the hiccup; it looks like it might not have info for all the qualified fields to be uploaded. From the error message, it looks like some data might have been downloaded to your machine.

Bethany

messages.subject: Re: Future models and how to classify a good distribution model?
messages.subject_clean: Future models and how to classify a good distribution model?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
To answer your first question, there is no "right" answer. Wallace offers several methods to evaluate model performance (as seen in your screenshot; area under the curve (AUC), continuous boyce index (CBI), omission rate (OR), AICc). One method is not better compared to another, you might even find one model performing well in one method and poorly with another. You can find information on the specifics of these methods in the Model component guidance text. Here you'll find info on each method and what values are optimal. Furthermore, you can also try several models and compare the predictions in regards to ecological realism- is one predicting areas you know the species is not known to be found? You mentioned the variables- you can find the variable response curves in the Response Curve module of the Visualize component.

As for the GCMs, WorldClim offers a variety of GCMs (General Circulation Models/Global Climate Models) at four different RCPs (Representative Concentration Pathways) that Wallace uses for future projections. Information on the different models can be found here https://worldclim.org/cmip6maps.html or https://www.worldclim.org/data/cmip6/cmip6climate.html. Please note, the usage of RCPs was recently replaced with Shared Socio-economic Pathways (SSPs), so you may see that in the literature instead.

I hope that information helps.
Bethany Johnson

messages.subject: Re: Error when uploading environmental rasters
messages.body_plain:
Hello to both,

This warning is just an indication that your environmental rasters have unidentical/unmatching pixels with NA values. You should be able to carry on with your analyses, however, this warning will prevent you from running the three modules within the 'Env Space' (Characterize Environmental Space) component. Wallace removes pixels with NA values where an occurrence record falls, so if multiple species are uploaded and the NA values don't match, it would crash. So to eliminate problems, we added the warning. If you'd like to run the Characterize Environmental space, I can give you code to process your rasters so the NA values match, although I wouldn't advise modeling with these rasters, as it is removing information in place of NA values.

I hope that settled your confusion and let me know if you are having any problems.

Bethany Johnson

messages.subject: Re: Problems with plotting
messages.body_plain:
I've had the same warning message when working with global rasters. When investigating further I noticed that the addRasterImage function can be set to allow for larger than 4MB images with the maxBytes argument. So support for larger images seems to be feasible at least.
